channel.description: Latest articles from The Valley Times-News (valleytimes-news.com)

item.title: Free food distribution set for Feb. 21
item.description: Valley Community Outreach will host a free food distribution Feb. 21, 10 a.m.–noon ET at Valley Sportsplex, first-come for Valley, West Point, Lanett and nearby residents.

item.title: BOE recognizes Amazing Shake competition winners
item.description: Chambers County BOE honors W.F. Burns Amazing Shake winners, hears proposal for a Montgomery internship, and approves staff cuts and the 2026-27 school calendar.

item.title: Margaret Scott Rollison
item.description: Margaret Scott Rollison entered into the presence of her Lord and Savior on January 26, 2026, passing peacefully at her home. She was born on March 30, 1960, in Langdale, Alabama, to William Henry Scott, Jr., and Eleanor Davis Scott. Margaret was raised in West Point, Georgia, where her faith was deeply rooted and nurtured as a lifelong member of West Point United Methodist Church. item.title: High school students participating in beauty expo
item.description: Local nonprofit Unite will host a free beauty expo Feb. 8 in Lanett, giving 25 LaFayette, Lanett and Valley High students hands-on lessons and career insight from makeup artist MaShondra Johnson.

item.title: Southern Union Foundation names two new members to board of directors
item.description: Southern Union Foundation adds Traci Henry and Darryl Wilkerson to its board, and names Kelli Hodge chair, Michael Williams vice chair and Carol Knight secretary/treasurer.

item.title: New Standing Rock community center almost complete
item.description: After nine years of fish fries and fundraisers, Standing Rock’s new community center nears completion and is hoped to be ready as a polling place for the 2026 primaries.

item.title: LaFayette faces a deadline for project commitment
item.description: Facing a one-month deadline to commit to a major waterline replacement or risk century‑old pipes under a state road project, LaFayette also reshaped trash bids and city ordinances.

item.title: Beulah varsity teams win big on Senior Night
item.description: The Beulah basketball teams put on dominant victories against Notasulga at home on Thursday to celebrate Senior Night.

item.title: 'DREAM COME TRUE:' Douglas Jones Jr. returns to the Bulldogs as head football coach
item.description: LaFayette native Douglas Jones Jr. has been named the new head football coach for the LaFayette Bulldogs, succeeding Juan Williams.

item.title: Riley discusses Valley construction projects
item.description: Mayor Riley outlines a busy 2026 for Valley, with new subdivisions, a school site, businesses and major road work planned as the city builds on stronger finances.
